text: Co-design partitions tasks by comparative advantage — linear algebra to photonics, nonlinearity and memory to electronics. If photonics accelerates the linear 90% of a workload by 100x, what caps the end-to-end speedup?
choices: About 9x, by Amdahl's law, because the un-accelerated 10% comes to dominate
1x, because the conversions cancel all benefit
explanation: Amdahl's law gives speedup <= 1 / (0.1 + 0.9/100), which is about 9x, no matter how fast the linear part runs. Choice 0 ignores the serial remainder; choice 2 is too pessimistic; choice 3 misapplies the fraction — speedup is bounded by the un-accelerated part, not proportional to the accelerated part.
